summary: Decided six-colourability of ONE periodic quotient at a = 1/5, the period lattice 4Z^2 (index 16). Result: UNSAT, sharply - the quotient is K_16, so this period needs all 16 colours. Exact Q(sqrt3), one process, under 2 s. (i) Window completeness by proof: forcedness forces 3 < N < 16.33, so F is exhausted by N in {4,7,9,12,13,16}; |F| = 42 on rings 6,12,6,6,12 with ring 16 empty, matching the saved artifact. (ii) No self-loops: F misses 4Z^2, whose nonzero norms are multiples of 16. (iii) The connection set S = F mod 4 is all 15 nonzero residues of (Z/4)^2, so the graph is complete. (iv) Independent adjacency check that never reads the list F: all 120 coset pairs scanned over their whole difference class with the strict criterion evaluated directly - 120/120 adjacent, 0 missing. (v) chi = 16; 6-colour backtracking with symmetry breaking is UNSAT, and all 8008 six-subsets of the 16 cosets contain an edge. Scope: this period and periods containing it only; the interior problem is already unsatisfiable, so no boundary rule or ring-3 tangency pair is involved; no other period swept; nothing bounds chi(R^2). Consequence without further search: every periodic proper colouring at a = 1/5 has index >= 19.

escalation: Precise obstacle: at a = 1/5 every period of index < 19 is now excluded, but exclusion at index 16 was by completeness of the quotient (K_16), a mechanism that weakens as the index grows - the quotient has more vertices and the same 15-residue connection set spread over them. No argument yet separates 'large index' from 'six-colourable', so the periodic route either needs a uniform obstruction (e.g. a counting or packing lemma valid for all period lattices, not a clique) or must accept that periodic candidates of large period cannot be excluded by quotient completeness. Expected useful output: a uniform lower bound on the chromatic number of Cay(Lambda, F) for all sublattice quotients at a = 1/5, or an explicit 6-colouring of one index-19 quotient with the full boundary check.
